questions.question: Explain how traders crossed the Indian Ocean to reach the East African coast.
questions.expected_answer: Traders from Arabia, Persia and India sailed wooden ships called dhows, with large triangular sails. They used the monsoon winds, which blow in one direction for part of the year and the opposite direction for another part, so they could sail to East Africa with one monsoon and home with the other.

questions.question: Name the main goods Mapungubwe exported and imported.
questions.expected_answer: Mapungubwe exported mainly gold and ivory, and probably animal skins and furs and perhaps copper. It imported mainly glass beads, many from India, and cotton cloth, and a few pieces of Chinese porcelain have been found.

questions.question: Explain how goods were carried to the coast and why this trade is called an early form of globalisation.
questions.expected_answer: There were no roads, wheeled carts or pack animals, and tsetse flies made using oxen difficult, so porters carried goods on their heads and shoulders along paths, often following rivers, on journeys of many weeks. The trade linked southern Africa with the East African coast, Arabia, India and China, connecting people across continents, which is an early form of globalisation.
